description:
Our Tamil language is beautified with literary beauty. It is not just a literature, but it is a language of divine. This can be provide by highlighting the story of Devara Moovar namely, Thirugnana Sambandar, Sundarar, Thirunavukarsar, Manickavasagarm Kandhasamy Swamigal etc. Kanda Swamy Swamigal have composed numerous bhakthi hymn which consists of literary, beauty and bhakthi rasa. Manicka Vasagar. Though there are number of hymns of Kandasamy Swamigal, the researcher who got impressed after hearing Karamadai Thalapuranam and Kaumara Madalayam in Coimbatore. Made up her mind to take  Kongu Naattu Kandhasamy Swamigalin Karaimadaith Thalapuranathil Naatuppadalap Paadalgal , for her research study. The researcher does not want such a valuable hymns to get prisoned to among four wall.
 		These hymns were some by Kandasamy Swamigal disciples and his followers verbally there were no notations nor proofs for this precious compositions of Kandasamy Swamigal. So the Researcher in her research study have given notation and a format for his compositions. Apart from that the researcher have taught to her student and will publish in the form at the book. The researcher selected some students from the Music department, Avinashilingam Institute for Home Science and Higher Education for Women, Coimbatore and taught them the Nattupada Padalgal of Kandasamy Swamigal and made them to perform twice at Kaumara Madalayam. 
 SinceKandasamy Swamigal belongs to Coimbatore district, the researcher starter her study by highlighting the poets who belongs to Coimbatore. The second chapter deals with life history of Kandasamy Swamigal. The researcher took Thalapurana as a third chapter, the researcher further leaded her research study by analyzing the literary beauties of Naatupadala Paadalgal of Karaimadaith Thalapuranam. The fourth chapter consists of notation of Naatupadala Paadalgal which is notated by the research. The researcher have done a detailed study on the grammar and the meaning of sahityam and its beauties of her fifth chapter.
